intent: I want to replace my Denver-area lawn with artificial turf this year. Can my HOA stop me, will my city let me put it in the front or back yard, does the 2026 drought change the choice between sod and turf, and will any rebate pay for it?
distinctValue: The national lawn page is generic, each town page carries one city's rule, and the HOA, turf-law and rebate guides are statewide or provider by provider. This page is a four-step placement guide that sorts the rules by what decides where turf can go on a lot, not by city, and links the town pages and guides for the detail instead of repeating it. Step 1, home type under C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5: detached homes get the backyard line in (1)(i.5), with the board's retained safety, fire-buffer and grading powers; a home that shares a wall falls under (1)(i), where the association 'shall not prohibit' nonvegetative turf grass but 'may restrict' it to rear yard locations; (1)(i.5)(VI)(B) expressly excludes condominiums. No other page sets out the attached-home and condo answers. Step 2, what the back fence faces: Arvada (not in public view, including streets, sidewalks, parks and trails) and Westminster (not adjacent to a street, park or open space) against Thornton (no limit out back), Brighton (listed in Table 8-1, with 8.04's 50% living ground cover) and Northglenn (six percent slope bar on existing single-family yards). Step 3, the front-yard share side by side: Arvada and Westminster none in a street-facing yard, Thornton 25% with tree equivalents, Brighton 20% of frontage with the 8.01 exemptions, Lafayette 75% live materials that single-family building permits must meet, and Aurora Water's 50% coverage maximum with no stated base. Step 4, the water provider: Denver Water's turf exclusion and allocated 2026 discounts, Thornton as the paying exception, and, for anyone weighing sod, Denver Water's stop on establishment permits after 30 September 2026 and Aurora's ban on new cool-weather turf. Rebate detail stays in the water rebates guide.

sources.label: C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5 (FindLaw copy)
sources.note: Rendered in headless Chromium on 12 September 2026. Page banner: 'Current as of January 01, 2025 | Updated by Findlaw Staff'. FindLaw is not the official publisher, so the page dates the wording to SB23-178 (session law below) and to this 1 January 2025 copy rather than calling it current text. Subsection (1)(i)(I)(A) applies only to a single-family home that shares one or more walls with another unit; (1)(i.5) applies only to a detached single-family home and expressly not to an attached home or a condominium.
supports: (1) Notwithstanding any provision in the declaration, bylaws, or rules and regulations of the association to the contrary, an association shall not prohibit any of the following:

(i)(I)(A) The use of xeriscape, nonvegetative turf grass, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes to provide ground covering to property for which a unit owner is responsible, including a limited common element or property owned by the unit owner. Associations may adopt and enforce design or aesthetic guidelines or rules that apply to nonvegetative turf grass and drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes or regulate the type, number, and placement of drought-tolerant plantings and hardscapes that may be installed on a unit owner's property or on a limited common element or other property for which the unit owner is responsible. An association may restrict the installation of nonvegetative turf grass to rear yard locations only.

This subsection (1)(i)(I)(A), as amended by Senate Bill 23-178, enacted in 2023, applies only to a unit that is a single-family home that shares one or more walls with another unit and does not apply to a unit that is a detached single-family home.
(A) Not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property;

(II) For the purposes of this subsection (1)(i.5), each association shall select at least three preplanned water-wise garden designs that are preapproved for installation in front yards within the common interest community.

(V) Nothing in this subsection (1)(i.5) shall be construed to prohibit or restrict the authority of associations to: (A) Adopt bona fide safety requirements consistent with applicable landscape codes or recognized safety standards for the protection of persons and property; (B) Prohibit or restrict changes that interfere with the establishment and maintenance of fire buffers or defensible spaces; or (C) Prohibit or restrict changes to existing grading, drainage, or other structural landscape elements necessary for the protection of persons and property.

(VI) Notwithstanding any provision of this section to the contrary, this subsection (1)(i.5) applies only to a unit that is a single-family detached home and does not apply to: (A) A unit that is a single-family attached home that shares one or more walls with another unit; or (B) A condominium.
Current as of January 01, 2025

supports: CHAPTER 207 ... SENATE BILL 23-178 ... AN ACT CONCERNING REMOVING BARRIERS TO WATER-WISE LANDSCAPING IN COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITIES.
SECTION 1. In Colorado Revised Statutes, 38-33.3-106.5, amend (1)(i)(I)(A); and add (1)(i.5) as follows:

An association may restrict the installation of nonvegetative turf grass to rear yard locations only. THIS SUBSECTION (1)(i)(I)(A), AS AMENDED BY SENATE BILL 23-178, ENACTED IN 2023, APPLIES ONLY TO A UNIT THAT IS A SINGLE-FAMILY HOME THAT SHARES ONE OR MORE WALLS WITH ANOTHER UNIT AND DOES NOT APPLY TO A UNIT THAT IS A DETACHED SINGLE-FAMILY HOME.

(VI) NOTWITHSTANDING ANY PROVISION OF THIS SECTION TO THE CONTRARY, THIS SUBSECTION (1)(i.5) APPLIES ONLY TO A UNIT THAT IS A SINGLE-FAMILY DETACHED HOME AND DOES NOT APPLY TO: (A) A UNIT THAT IS A SINGLE-FAMILY ATTACHED HOME THAT SHARES ONE OR MORE WALLS WITH ANOTHER UNIT; OR (B) A CONDOMINIUM.

sources.label: Thornton Water: 2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate (PDF)
sources.note: Downloaded and read with pdftotext on 12 September 2026. Every page footer reads 1/1/2026. The page does not repeat the rebate amounts (they are in the water rebates guide and the Thornton page), and does not mention the product fade requirement.
supports: Rear Yard & Enclosed Side Yards: Artificial turf allowed with no limitations.
All Other Areas: Artificial turf shall not exceed 25% of the landscape area. (Front and unenclosed Side yards not occupied by driveways, sidewalks, patios, decks, buildings, or other structures)
A Minor Development Permit is required before the installation of artificial turf as landscaping.
Living plant materials are required when artificial turf is installed in the lot's front or unenclosed side yard landscape areas.
One tree equivalent is required for the first 750 square feet of artificial turf or a fraction thereof.
One-half tree equivalent is required for each additional 250 square feet of artificial turf or a fraction thereof.
The residential water-wise landscape rebate provides up to $2 per square foot for qualifying 200 – 1,000 square feet projects. The rebate has a lifetime maximum of $2,000 per residential lot.

To be eligible for the rebate, artificial turf must replace an area of high-water demand lawn, such as Kentucky Bluegrass, on existing residential lots or areas of no landscaping on new construction residential lots.

supports: Effective immediately, Aurora is in a Stage 1 drought. Watering restrictions are in place.
No watering permitted between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. No new cool-weather turf can be installed.
Why doesn't Aurora Water provide rebates to convert 100% to artificial turf?

While artificial turf doesn't require any water, it is not water-wise landscape. Aurora residents are permitted to install artificial turf, subject to a 50% coverage maximum, but the city of Aurora does not incentivize those installations.
New sod is not allowed during Stage 1 restrictions unless it meets Aurora's low-water use requirements.

supports: Prohibits a local entity, on and after January 1, 2026, from installing, planting, or placing, or allowing any person to install, plant, or place, any nonfunctional turf, nonfunctional artificial turf, or invasive plant species, as part of a new development project or redevelopment project, on applicable property within the local entity's jurisdiction;

unresolved: Whether a 2025 or 2026 act changed C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5 (1)(i) or (1)(i.5) was not confirmed. Both FindLaw copies are current as of 1 January 2025; the official C.R.S. files on content.leg.colorado.gov returned 403; Justia returned a blocked page; and the legislature's bill search ignored its session and text filters, returning a generic list of 2026 signed bills (one a Division of Real Estate sunset bill whose text was not checked). The page therefore dates the wording to SB23-178 and FindLaw's 1 January 2025 copy and tells the reader to cite the section when asking the board for a written position.

Subsection (1)(i.5)(VI)(B) expressly excludes condominiums from the detached-home rule, but neither text says in terms whether (1)(i) reaches a condominium unit. The page only states the express exclusion and sends condo owners to the association for its written rules.

Aurora Water's '50% coverage maximum' names no base area, and the current Aurora UDO could not be opened (see aurora-co evidence). The page tells the reader to get the answer from Aurora Planning in writing.

Whether Brighton's 20% frontage cap reaches a re-landscape of an existing detached house depends on the Section 8.01 exemptions and Residential Design Review; the page sends the reader to Community Development.

Whether a landscaping change at an existing Lafayette home needs a building permit that brings in 26-19-5(d)(3) was not confirmed, and the replacement land use code's final vote was scheduled for 15 September 2026. Recheck the Lafayette Listens page after that date.
Westminster's Unified Development Code was still called proposed in the 2 March 2026 presentation; no adoption was found. The FAQ says updated regulations are prospective.
The City and County of Denver's own zoning treatment of turf on an existing home was not researched; the page makes no claim about it and lists Denver only as a nearby town page.

Drought rules change. Denver Water's stop on establishment permits runs 'until further notice' from 30 September 2026, and Aurora's Stage 1 page carries no declaration date. Both are dated on the page; recheck after 30 September 2026.
